content:
Multiple stores under Asia International Catering Group withdraw applications

It has only been a few days since the new measures came into effect, and a chain restaurant has already "backed out." Among them, the "100% Restaurant" with 12 branches approved only mentioned on social media platforms that 8 branches allowed dogs to enter. The Ma On Shan Kam Ying Court branch posted a handwritten notice last Friday (the 10th) stating "This store has cancelled its dog-friendly restaurant status," which was later replaced with a sign saying "Please do not bring pets inside." The "Milk Cafe" under the same group also had 13 branches approved, but social media only mentioned 12. The original "Eatago Restaurant" at Tsui Ping (North) Shopping Mall in Kwun Tong has also disappeared from the FEHD's updated list dated July 11.

The Asia International Catering Group to which the above restaurants belong posted on social media last Saturday (the 11th) stating that after assessment, due to factors such as store space, seating layout, entrance and exit traffic flow, and customer flow in certain branches, allowing dogs to enter might affect other customers' dining experience, on-site order, and safety. To ensure all customers enjoy a comfortable and safe dining environment as the primary consideration, they decided to proactively apply for cancellation of the relevant permits for individual branches; if individual branches have suitable conditions, they do not rule out reapplying.

The group confirmed in response to media inquiries that the "100% Restaurant" branches at Tseung Kwan O Ming Tak Shopping Mall, Fanling Yat Fai Plaza, and Nam Cheong V WALK are handling cancellation procedures. Staff at the Milk Cafe Tuen Mun Times Square branch also told reporters that due to supporting facility issues they could not accommodate dogs and had returned the licence.

In addition, McDonald's, which originally had four approved branches, previously told the media that the official launch date and details would be announced later. Checking the latest list, the Yau Tong Yau Lai Shopping Mall branch has disappeared. Also missing are the Li Chi Kok Manhattan Mall "One Bowl Noodle," the Le Méridien Cyberport South House in Cyberport, Mong Kok Buda Two, and the shuttered Sha Tin Alva Hotel restaurant Yat Hin and Alva House, bringing the cumulative total of restaurants removed from the list to 9. Moreover, Café de Coral, which had two approved branches, had a notice stating that the pet-friendly arrangement would be postponed until 3 p.m. today (the 13th). Reporters observed on-site that the Tai Wai Wai Fong Café de Coral would be delayed by seven days until the 20th of this month, while the Tsuen Wan Lok Yau Kui Café de Coral launched as usual today; reporters waited from 5:30 p.m. to 7:30 p.m. and did not see any dog owners bringing their pets.

M+ and Tseung Kwan O Plaza restaurants withdraw due to venue issues

Some restaurants had to cancel due to deed of mutual covenant and venue clause issues. Nodi, a café located in the basement of M+, applied to the FEHD to withdraw on its own because the M+ museum venue rules expressly prohibit dogs other than service dogs from entering, and the restaurant had to withdraw. In addition, Tseung Kwan O Plaza originally had three restaurants—Café de Coral, Ginsan Shanghai Sheng Jian Huang, and Oliver's Super Sandwiches—on the list, but they were removed on the eve of the policy's launch. The property management company responded to the media that the building's deed of mutual covenant does not allow dogs to enter the mall premises, so diners cannot bring dogs into the restaurants inside the mall. However, the media discovered a pet grooming shop inside the mall.

Restaurants warned for open-flame cooking on dining tables

In addition, some approved restaurants were found to be in violation. According to media reports, at least two restaurants that allow dogs used open-flame appliances to cook or heat food on dining tables. After inspection, the FEHD immediately issued stern warnings, ordering them not to repeat the offence, reiterating that the licence condition is "no cooking or heating of food on dining tables at any time," and stressed that if the conditions and legal requirements are violated again, enforcement will be taken immediately. Other restaurants engaging in similar behaviour will also be subject to immediate enforcement action without a grace period.

Some restaurants impose time slots and quantity restrictions, no dogs on weekends

FEHD guidelines state that restaurants may, as needed, set their own time slots and areas for allowing dogs to enter. Some pet-friendly restaurants have restrictions on dog access. A "100% Restaurant" branch's notice states that dogs cannot be accommodated from 11:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday to Sunday, and from 6 p.m. to 8 p.m., with a maximum of 3 dogs allowed. If neighbouring diners feel uneasy, the dog must be placed back on the ground; if a dog barks excessively, it must be calmed or taken away; if staff need to clean up excrement, an additional cleaning fee of HK$100 will be charged. A "Milk Cafe" branch also posted a similar notice stating that dogs are not accommodated from 11:30 a.m. to 6:30 p.m., Monday to Friday, nor all day on Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays. Another restaurant stated that bringing dogs requires a WhatsApp reservation.

The new measures have sparked controversy. Multiple photos circulating online show dog owners allowing their dogs to lick utensils directly and letting dogs place their front paws on dining tables. Many netizens left comments saying "I won't patronise" under posts from restaurants announcing they would allow dogs. A Kowloon City district restaurant said it received nearly 30 complaints on the first day of implementation. FEHD Director Yuen Yuk-kin said today that 20 complaints have been received so far, involving issues such as dog leash length and where dogs are seated. The department has conducted around 2,300 inspections and issued a certain number of verbal warnings.
